summary: Feed s185_triple is degraded: 83.3% encrypted traffic exceeds IDS 60% tolerance, required VLAN 20 is missing (48% untagged), and 9.1% TCP packet drops exceed 1% threshold - all reduce IDS detection coverage.

findings.root_cause: 83.3% of bytes are encrypted vs IDS tolerance of 60%; traffic is opaque to IDS without decryption, likely TLS forwarded without SSL visibility.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS requires full payload for signature and anomaly detection; encrypted payloads cannot be inspected, blinding detection for 83% of traffic and allowing threats to hide in TLS.

recommended_fix.why: IDS needs cleartext payload; decrypting at packet broker/SSL visibility appliance or filtering to only forward decryptable traffic restores inspection capability within 60% tolerance.

findings.root_cause: Required VLAN 20 not seen and 48% of packets are untagged; packet broker or TAP/SPAN trunk is stripping 802.1Q tags or not forwarding VLAN 20.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS requires VLANs 10 and 20 for segmentation-aware policies; missing VLAN 20 means ~50% of expected traffic is invisible or misclassified, creating coverage gap for that segment.

recommended_fix.why: Preserving and forwarding 802.1Q tags for VLANs 10 and 20 ensures IDS receives complete, correctly segmented traffic for policy enforcement.

findings.root_cause: 9.1% of TCP packets (264/2900) show gaps/retransmissions indicating drops in SPAN or packet broker due to oversubscription/congestion before the IDS 1Gbps port.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS needs both directions and full streams for TCP reassembly; 9% loss causes broken flows, missed signatures, and evasion - IDS cannot reliably detect attacks.

recommended_fix.why: Distributing traffic across multiple IDS instances/ports or reducing oversubscription prevents buffer drops and delivers complete flows to the IDS.
